answer: A per-identity bond that is slashed, not merely staked, is the concrete Sybil defence: each address locks a minimum it forfeits in full if any sock-puppet in its cluster is caught double-signing. A crystal-clear ledger ties every key to one cluster, so a farm of N identities needs N separate locks plus N times the slashed bleed, while honest payout stays flat. A cheap key is easy to register, but the anchor is the loss on each clone: the cedar of evidence makes cost grow linearly while reward does not.
